what: Kinsale writes excess and surplus lines insurance: cover for risks standard insurers decline, such as unusual commercial property, contractors and small specialty exposures, underwritten entirely on its own technology.
customers: Wholesale brokers bringing hard-to-place risks from retail agents.
moat: Everything is underwritten in-house on its own systems, with no delegated authority to agents, which gives it better data and a far lower expense ratio than competitors.
risks: Specialty insurance pricing is softening after several very profitable years
The analyst average target is about 10% below the current price
Growth has been exceptional, and that is hard to sustain as the company gets larger
opportunities: A 26.9% net margin and $973M of free cash flow on $2.0B of revenue
Revenue grew from $654M to $1.9B in four years
Its combined ratio is among the best in American insurance, which means it earns money on underwriting, not just investments
watch: The combined ratio and gross written premium growth.
